theme: 3 terms for VoiceOver in SwiftUI: the spoken reading, the grouped item and the custom command

terms.definition: A modifier that tells VoiceOver the current value of a control, such as 50 percent.
terms.example: Add an Accessibility Value, so VoiceOver reads the percent.

terms.definition: A modifier that groups child views into one item for VoiceOver.
terms.example: Make the row one Accessibility Element, so VoiceOver reads it once.

terms.definition: A modifier that adds a custom action that VoiceOver users can choose on a view.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to improve VoiceOver in SwiftUI: Accessibility Value, Accessibility Element & Accessibility Action, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Accessibility Value - A modifier that tells VoiceOver the current value of a control, such as 50 percent.
Accessibility Element - A modifier that groups child views into one item for VoiceOver.
Accessibility Action - A modifier that adds a custom action that VoiceOver users can choose on a view.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: SwiftUI Accessibility Value, Accessibility Element & Accessibility Action | Day 166
landscape.description:
Explain Accessibility Value, Accessibility Element & Accessibility Action in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
접근성 값, 접근성 엘리먼트, 접근성 액션 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Accessibility Value - A modifier that tells VoiceOver the current value of a control, such as 50 percent.
한국어: 접근성 값: 50퍼센트처럼 컨트롤의 현재 값을 VoiceOver에게 알려 주는 수정자

Accessibility Element - A modifier that groups child views into one item for VoiceOver.
한국어: 접근성 엘리먼트: 자식 뷰들을 VoiceOver용 하나의 항목으로 묶어 주는 수정자

Accessibility Action - A modifier that adds a custom action that VoiceOver users can choose on a view.
한국어: 접근성 액션: VoiceOver 사용자가 뷰에서 고를 수 있는 사용자 지정 동작을 추가하는 수정자

landscape.hook: Can you explain Accessibility Value, Accessibility Element and Accessibility Action in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, VoiceOver reads my volume row as two separate items.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Group them with an Accessibility Element. It makes the child views one item for VoiceOver.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used `.combine`, and now it reads Volume 50 together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. But the user does not know the unit yet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I add an Accessibility Value, like fifty percent?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. An Accessibility Value tells VoiceOver the current value of a control.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now, a user wants to mute without opening the screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add an Accessibility Action. It is a custom action that a VoiceOver user can choose on the view.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Name every Accessibility Action clearly, because VoiceOver reads the name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should I test with VoiceOver on a device?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Always. The Accessibility Element and the Accessibility Value need real listening tests.
